ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a gray square sheet of paper, with a black boundary, and the problem states to cut this square sheet of paper into two pieces with one straight line. Reasoning: A single straight-line cut can only produce one new straight edge on the boundary of the square. If the straight line connects two adjacent sides, it usually cuts out a triangle, and the other piece is a polygon; if the straight line connects two opposite sides, it produces shapes such as rectangles or trapezoids. If one wants one of the pieces itself to become a smaller square, it needs to have four equal and mutually perpendicular sides, of which three must come from the boundary of the original square, and the other one from the cutting line. In this way, only when the cutting line is parallel to the original side and cuts out a part with the same length as the original side is it possible to form a square, but that would equal the original whole sheet of paper and cannot at the same time leave a second nonempty piece of paper. Therefore, when using one straight line to cut a square into two pieces, it is not possible to cut one of the pieces into a square.

raw_record.question_text: A square piece of paper is cut in a straight line into two pieces. What shape cannot be created as one of the resulting pieces?

method.method_draft: Use the single straight-cut constraint. Read from the image that the starting paper is a square. Read from the text that exactly one straight-line cut divides it into two pieces and ask which shape cannot be one resulting piece. Reason by cases: a straight line crossing a square can connect adjacent sides, producing a triangle and a remaining polygon, or connect opposite sides, producing rectangles/trapezoids. To obtain a smaller square as one piece, the cut would need to form one complete side of that square while the other three sides come from the original square boundary; the only possible axis-aligned square would have to have the full original side length, leaving no second piece. Therefore a square cannot be one of the two nonempty pieces.

推理：一次直线切割只能在正方形边界上产生一条新的直线边。如果直线连接相邻两边，通常会切出一个三角形，另一块是多边形；如果直线连接相对两边，会产生矩形或梯形等形状。若想让其中一块本身成为一个较小的正方形，它需要有四条相等且互相垂直的边，其中三条必须来自原正方形边界，另一条来自切割线。这样只有切割线平行于原边并切出与原边长相同的部分时才可能形成正方形，但那会等于原来的整张纸，不能同时留下第二块非空纸片。因此，一条直线把正方形切成两块时，不能把其中一块切成正方形。
